newsitem.title: UK: DBS Management does not know of any PIA fine.
newsitem.headline: DBS Management does not know of any PIA fine.

text.p: Business support services group DBS Management Plc said on Monday it "has no knowledge" of any fine to be imposed on it by the Personal Investment Authority (PIA) over alleged pensions mis-selling.

DBS was responding to an article in Monday's Independent newspaper which said a 500,000 stg fine -- which would be the largest given by the PIA for a rule breach -- was in the final stages of being agreed by the financial services regulator.
The group said in a statement that while it did not know of any fine it "considers its resources are adequate to cover such a penalty in the event of it being confirmed".

DBS confirmed its commitment to ensure that any investors who purchased personal pensions through its members are properly dealt with under the terms of the pensions review by financial watchdog the Securities and Investments Board (SIB).
DBS reiterated that it has made "substantial" provisions to cover the costs of accelerating the review.
The Independent said the fine would be an embarrassment to DBS chairman Ken Davy, who sits on the PIA board.
Shares in DBS were down 27-1/2 pence at 1,117-1/2 at 0735 GMT.
